newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian mergers and acquisitions rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italian mergers and acquisitions rise in 1996.

text.p: The number of mergers and acquisitions involving Italian companies rose by 24 percent to 652 in 1996 and were worth a total of 55 trillion lire, including share buy offers for a value of 12 trillion lire.
KPMG said in a survey report that activity had shrunk between 1991 and 1995 but the number of operations in 1996 rose to levels last seen in 1991.
The financial markets were starting to play an important role in the merger and acquisitions sector with four out of the 10 top operations completed on the stock exchange.

The engineering and electrical sector saw an upswing in activity, notably Fincantieri's takoever of New Sulzer Diesel and the purchase of Avir by Owens Illinois, accounting for 14 percent of the value of all operations.

The biggest deal of the year was the sale of 15.8 percent of state oil group ENI to private and institutional investors for 8.8 trillion lire followed by the placement of 31.8 percent of insurer INA for 3.26 billion lire.
The flotation of 23.8 percent of broadcasting group Mediaset also raised 1.957 trillion and was the third largest operation.

U.S. companies were involved in 50 deals, French in 26, British in 22 and German companies in 18. Italian companies were most active in France and Germany, pulling off 16 and 14 merger deals or acquisition deals respectively. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
